title: 2 Kings 19
paragraphs: ¹ When King Hezekiah heard the report, he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the LORD's temple. ² He sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests — all wearing sackcloth — to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. ³ They said to him, "Hezekiah says: This is a day of distress and humiliation and disgrace — like a woman in labor who has no strength to deliver. ⁴ Perhaps the LORD your God has heard all the words of the field commander, whom his master the king of Assyria sent to mock the living God. Perhaps the LORD your God will rebuke him for what he has heard. Offer a prayer for the remnant that still survives." ⁵ So King Hezekiah's officials came to Isaiah.

⁶ Isaiah replied to them, "Tell your master: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of what you have heard — those words with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me. ⁷ I am going to put a spirit in him so that when he hears a certain report, he will return to his own country, and there I will have him cut down by the sword.'" ⁸ So the field commander withdrew, and when he found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, he learned that the king had left Lachish. ⁹ Then Sennacherib received word that Tirhakah king of Cush had set out to fight against him. So he sent messengers to Hezekiah again with this message: ¹⁰ "Say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let the god you trust in deceive you when he says, 'Jerusalem will not be given into the hands of the king of Assyria.'"

¹¹ "You yourself have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the countries — they destroyed them completely. And will you be saved? ¹² Did the gods of the nations that my fathers destroyed rescue them — the gods of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Tel Assar? ¹³ Where is the king of Hamath? Where is the king of Arpad? Where is the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, or of Ivah?" ¹⁴ Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the LORD's temple and spread it out before the LORD. ¹⁵ Hezekiah prayed to the LORD: "LORD, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth."

¹⁶ "LORD, bend down your ear and listen. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib, who sent this message to mock the living God. ¹⁷ It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste to all these nations and their lands. ¹⁸ They have thrown the gods of those nations into the fire and burned them up, because they were not real gods — only wood and stone, shaped by human hands. So of course they could be destroyed. ¹⁹ But now, LORD our God, please deliver us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you alone, LORD, are God." ²⁰ Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I have heard your prayer concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria."

²¹ This is what the LORD has declared about him: The virgin daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head at you. ²² Who is it you have insulted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in arrogance? Against the Holy One of Israel. ²³ Through your messengers you have taunted the LORD, saying, "With my countless chariots I have climbed to the heights of the mountains, to the far reaches of Lebanon. I have felled its tallest cedars, its finest pines. I have reached its remotest peaks, its thickest forests. ²⁴ I have dug wells in foreign lands and drunk their waters. By the soles of my own feet I have dried up every river of Egypt." ²⁵ Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained this. In ancient times I planned it, and now I have brought it to pass — that you should turn fortified cities into piles of rubble.

²⁶ Therefore their people were powerless; they were shattered and ashamed. They were like grass in the field, like tender green shoots, like grass on a rooftop, scorched before it can grow. ²⁷ But I know where you live and where you go and come from, and I know your rage against me. ²⁸ Because your fury against me and your arrogance have reached my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bridle in your mouth, and I will make you turn back the way you came. ²⁹ And this will be the sign for you: this year you will eat what grows on its own, and the next year what springs up from that. But in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit. ³⁰ The surviving remnant of the house of Judah will once again take root below and bear fruit above.

³¹ For a remnant will go out from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will accomplish this. ³² Therefore this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow here. He will not come before it with shield or build a siege ramp against it. ³³ By the way he came, by that same way he will return. He will not enter this city, says the LORD. ³⁴ For I will defend this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David. ³⁵ That very night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the Assyrian camp. When the survivors got up the next morning, they found nothing but corpses everywhere.

³⁶ So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned home and stayed in Nineveh. ³⁷ One day, while he was worshipping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword and escaped to the land of Armenia. And his son Esarhaddon became king in his place.
